senses.gloss: , m. (accubitum, ἀκκούβιτον) dining couch of the Roman nobility of the imperial period in place of the older triclinium.
units: Lev. R. s. 7 מיסב על א׳ וכ׳ (Pesik. Eth. Korb. p. 61ᵃ הקוביטין; Yalk. Num. 777 איק׳; ib. Lev. 479 קוב׳, קנב׳; ib. Ps. 791 הננ׳ &c., corr. acc.; Pesik. R. s. 16, p. 83ᵇ ed. Fr. הקובטין) reclining on his accubitum.—לחם א׳, or ריפתא (ד)א׳ bread used at the meals of the nobility, fine bread.

<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Genesis 40:16">Targ. Y. II, Gen. XL, 16</cite> <he>ריפתא קקבטון</he> (read <he>ריפתא דאקקובטון</he>) bread of the nobles (h. text <cite ref="H01668"><he>חרי</he></cite>). Pesik. R. l. c. p. 82ᵃ (ref. to <he>לחם הפחה</he> <cite ref="Nehemiah 5:18">Neh. V, 18</cite>) <he>הקקבטין</he> sub. <cite ref="L00363"><he>לחם</he></cite>; Pesik. l. c. p. 59ᵃ <cite ref="S01861"><he>קקבטון</he></cite> (corr. acc.).
